Threat.value: I feel on guard even inside my own home
Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame
Being superalert or watchful or on guard

Memory.value: When I think about the frightening event I can sometimes smell things that I smelt when the frightening event happened.
When I remember the frightening event I feel like it is happening right now.
My memories of the event feel more real and vivid than memories of ordinary things

Negative Appraisals.value: I have lost my faith in people, life, or a higher power
The world is a dangerous place
My body keeps reacting as if I am still in danger even when I am safe

issues.item: Humiliation: I feel permanently humiliated by what happened
issues.explanation: For a life-threatening illness trauma, 'permanently humiliated' is hard to reconcile unless the illness involved a specifically shaming interpersonal circumstance; nothing else in the profile suggests that context. The other items center danger, fear, vivid reliving, and generalized threat, so humiliation stands out as clinically mismatched to the trauma type.

vignette: John, a 78-year-old retired Database Administrator from North America, has been struggling with the aftermath of a life-threatening illness that occurred several years ago. The traumatic event left him feeling on guard even within his own home and haunted by vivid memories of the experience. John recalls the hospital environment in stark detail, particularly the smell of antiseptic and sterile cleaning agents. Whenever these scents come to mind, they trigger a sense of reliving the frightening event, making it feel as if he is back in that moment again. The olfactory recall not only brings back the sights and sounds but also plunges him into the same intense negative emotions—fear, horror, anger, guilt, and shame—that accompanied his illness. These memories are so vivid and real that John often feels as though he has never truly left the hospital. He describes how his body remains hyperalert, reacting with fear even in safe environments. This hypervigilance is a constant reminder of the danger he faced and continues to perceive around him. As a result, John’s trust in the world and its people has eroded significantly. The memory of his illness, accompanied by the vivid smells and sensations, reinforces his belief that the world is indeed a dangerous place. He struggles with faith, not only in others but also in any higher power he once believed in. John's hypervigilance extends to even mundane activities at home. When working on minor tasks around the house, he feels as if he needs to be constantly alert and watchful. This heightened state of awareness makes him feel as though his body is still under threat, despite being safe now. The lingering sense of danger exacerbates his negative appraisals; it reinforces his belief that life is unpredictable and perilous. The cumulative effect of these symptoms has led John into a cycle where he feels perpetually trapped in the grip of fear and suspicion. His hypervigilance makes him wary even within familiar settings, causing him to doubt the safety of his own home—a place he once considered a sanctuary. As a retired Database Administrator, John used to enjoy organizing digital files with ease, but now he finds it difficult to focus on these tasks due to his constant state of alertness and intrusive memories. What finally brought John to seek help was a recent incident where the smell of cleaning products in a store triggered an intense panic attack. He realized that his quality of life had diminished significantly; he could no longer enjoy simple pleasures without being overwhelmed by fear. His most pressing concern is regaining a sense of safety and control over his thoughts and emotions. John hopes to find ways to mitigate these distressing symptoms, especially the persistent negative appraisals and hypervigilance that continue to dominate his daily life. In therapy, John has begun to explore how his memories contribute to his negative beliefs about the world and himself. Understanding this connection is key for him in working towards a more balanced perspective and finding ways to manage his symptoms effectively. He expresses hope for relief from the constant fear and an opportunity to reclaim some peace of mind in his golden years.
